hypothesis: If the starship.html ledger panel renders both SHIPPED governance verdicts and cum_hash 'chain OK' integrity signals via the same class (.lv.g → --g:#00ff41), a viewer cannot distinguish a MAYOR-signed governance outcome from a structural hash-validity check — violating the one-meaning-per-color rule.
summary: starship.html ledger source panel (L557–L593) renders eight values in .lv.g (CSS L55: .lv.g{color:var(--g)}; L11: --g:#00ff41). Three are governance verdicts — status SHIPPED (L563, L570) and 'SHIP · 29/29 tests GREEN' (L584). Five are hash-chain integrity signals — 'chain OK · +1' on cum_hash rows (L565, L572, L579, L586, L593). Source Atlas Doctrine reserves green exclusively for governance-ADMITTED; chain validity is a structural/observational property (hash verified ≈ 🔵 OBSERVED / MONO receipt voice), not a verdict. The collision is highest-stakes on L579: a NO_SHIP entry (L578, .lv.r) still shows its cum_hash in ADMITTED-green, so a rejected entry carries green in the same row block. --c (#00e5ff, cyan) is already used in the panel for entry ids (.lv.c) as the structural/receipt voice and is the natural slot for chain-validity. File declares authority=false (L171: 'NO RECEIPT · authority=false · action required').
